problems.title: Difference of two special sines
problems.question: Find sin75°−sin15°.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: sin A−sin B=2cos((A+B)/2)sin((A−B)/2).
steps: The value is 2cos45°sin30°=√2/2.

problems.title: Sum of two squares
problems.question: Evaluate(sin17+cos17)²+(sin17−cos17)².
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: (u+v)²+(u−v)²=2(u²+v²).
steps: Use sin²17+cos²17=1 to obtain2.

problems.title: Range of a shifted absolute value
problems.question: Find the range of|sin2α+cos3β−5|+4.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: With independent α,β, the sum sin2α+cos3β ranges over[−2,2].
steps: Subtracting5 gives[−7,−3]. Its absolute value ranges[3,7], then adding4 gives[7,11].

problems.title: Euler’s polyhedron relation
problems.question: A polyhedron’s edge count is twice its vertex count and 9 more than its face count. Find edges.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: E=2V, F=E−9, and V−E+F=2.
steps: Substitution gives E/2−9=2, so E=22.
problems.note: The standard convex (sphere-type) polyhedron convention is used.

problems.title: Projection of a proper trapezoid
problems.question: Which listed figure can be an orthogonal projection of a trapezoid:segment, triangle, square, rectangle?
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: A nondegenerate planar projection is an invertible affine map, which preserves parallelism and cannot turn a proper trapezoid into a parallelogram.
steps: A projection onto a plane perpendicular to the trapezoid’s plane can collapse it to a segment. No triangle arises from an invertible map or a rank1 collapse.
problems.note: A proper trapezoid is intended; rectangles are excluded from its definition.

problems.title: A missing zero answer
problems.question: Evaluate[2cos88°cos2°−cos86°]/cos86°.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: 2cos88°cos2°=cos90°+cos86°=cos86°.
steps: The numerator is 0 and the denominator is nonzero, so the quotient is 0.
problems.answer: 0; none of the listed expressions matches.
problems.note: The printed numerical choices omit0, and the three listed trigonometric alternatives are also nonzero.

problems.title: Product-to-sum cancellation
problems.question: Find cos8α+cos6α+2sin5αsin3α if sinα=1/√3.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: 2sin5αsin3α=cos2α−cos8α. Thus the expression is cos6α+cos2α.
steps: cos2α=1−2/3=1/3. Then cos6α=4cos³2α−3cos2α=−23/27.

problems.title: A four-factor trigonometric product
problems.question: Evaluate cos(π/24)cos(7π/24)sin(π/24)sin(7π/24).
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: Pair sine and cosine at each angle:the product is(1/4)sin15°sin105°.
steps: Product-to-sum gives sin15°sin105°=[cos90°−cos120°]/2=1/4. Thus the result is 1/16.

problems.title: Prism faces from diagonal count
problems.question: A prism has 130 space diagonals. Find its face count.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has n(n−3) space diagonals.
steps: n²−3n−130=(n−13)(n+10)=0, so n=13. Its face count is n+2=15.

problems.title: Height of a rhombus-based right prism
problems.question: A right prism has rhombus side 5 and space diagonals9,7. Find height.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: The squared base diagonals sum 4·5²=100. Each space diagonal squared adds h².
steps: Thus 9²+7²=100+2h², so h²=15.

problems.title: Cancellation does not restore excluded extrema
problems.question: Find the greatest value of y=(3−sinα)cos²α/cos²α.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: On its domain cosα≠0, the function simplifies to 3−sinα. This domain excludes sinα=±1.
steps: Hence its range is(2,4). Values approach4, but4 is never attained.
problems.answer: There is no greatest value; the supremum is 4.

problems.title: Order signed trigonometric values
problems.question: Order A=5sin200°, B=cos49°, C=5tan100°, D=tan240° increasingly.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
steps: Therefore C<A<B<D.

problems.title: Common period of a quotient and a sine
problems.question: Find the least common positive period of[sin(2x/3)+sin(x/2)]/sin(7x/12) and sin(x/5).
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: The quotient simplifies to 2cos(x/12), while retaining holes at x=12kπ/7. Its least period is 24π; the holes also repeat under that shift.
steps: The other function’s least period is 10π. The least common multiple of 24π and 10π is 120π.

problems.title: Surface area of a right prism
problems.question: A right prism base is a trapezoid tangent to a radius 2 circle, with midline6. Prism height is 6. Find total are a.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: Base altitude=4, base are a=6·4=24. A tangential quadrilateral has are a=r·semiperimeter, so perimeter=2·24/2=24.
steps: Lateral are a=24·6=144; add2 bases48 to obtain192.

problems.title: Oblique prism with all edges6
problems.question: A triangular prism has all edges6, and one upper vertex projects to the lower equilateral base’s incenter. Find lateral are a.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: The lateral edge’s horizontal projection has length base circumradius2√3. Vertical height=√(36−12)=2√6.
steps: For the two faces adjacent to that base vertex, the perpendicular horizontal component is the base inradius√3. Each face are a is 6√(24+3)=18√3.
For the third face, the horizontal perpendicular component is 2√3, so its are a is 6√(24+12)=36. Total36√3+36.

problems.title: Which inequalities hold for every acute angle?
problems.question: On0<α<π/2, check I sinα+cosα≤√2; II sinα+cosα≥√(2sin2α); III sinα+cosα≤√(2cos2α); IV sinα+cosα≤2tanα.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: I follows from(sinα+cosα)²=1+sin2α≤2. For II, both sides are nonnegative, and squaring gives 1+sin2α≥2sin2α.
steps: II is true because sin2α≤1. III fails at π/4 and is not real on part of the interval. IV fails for sufficiently small positive α.

problems.title: Squeezing an intersection to one point
problems.question: For a∈(−8π,8π), what is the maximum intersection count of y=3sin(4x−5) and y=(x−a)²+3?
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: The sine graph is≤3, while the parabola is≥3.
steps: Equality requires x=a and sin(4a−5)=1. Suitable a in the allowed interval exist, but at most this single x can work.

problems.title: Fourth-angle sine from tangent
problems.question: Find sin4α if tan(π+α)=−3.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: tanα=−3. Then sin2α=2tanα/(1+tan²α)=−3/5 and cos2α=(1−tan²α)/(1+tan²α)=−4/5.
steps: sin4α=2sin2αcos2α=24/25.

problems.title: Lateral area from a normal section
problems.question: Two lateral faces of an oblique triangular prism are perpendicular. Their common lateral edge is 12 and is 8,15 from the other lateral edges. Find lateral are a.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: A section perpendicular to all lateral edges is a right triangle with legs8,15, hypotenuse17. Its perimeter is 40.
steps: The prism’s lateral are a equals lateral-edge length times normal-section perimeter:12·40=480.

problems.title: Angle between hexagonal-prism lines
problems.question: A regular hexagonal prism has base side √3, height 1. Find the cosine between BF₁ and CD₁.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: Choose coordinates giving BF₁=(0,−3,1), CD₁=(−√3/2,−3/2,1). Their lengths are √10 and 2.
steps: The dot product is 9/2+1=11/2. The cosine is(11/2)/(2√10)=11/(4√10).

problems.title: Pair complementary tangent factors
problems.question: Evaluate∏ from k=1 to 45 of(1+tan k°).
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: For1≤k≤44, pair k with 45−k. Tangent subtraction gives(1+tan k°)(1+tan(45°−k°))=2.
steps: There are 22 such pairs, giving2²². The remaining45° factor is 2, so the total is 2²³.

problems.title: A bounded sine-addition expression
problems.question: Maximize x√(1−y²)+y√(1−x²).
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: The real domain is −1≤x, y≤1. Put x=sin u, y=sin v with principal angles u, v∈[−π/2,π/2].
steps: The radicals are cosu, cosv, and the expression is sin(u+v)≤1. Equality holds at x=y=1/√2.

problems.title: Represent a function with sine and cosine
problems.question: For which f among tanx, sin²x, sinxcosx, x²+3x can functions p, q satisfy f=p sinx+q cosx on the stated domain?
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: For any defined f, choose p(x)=f(x)sinx and q(x)=f(x)cosx.
steps: Then p sinx+q cosx=f(sin²x+cos²x)=f. This works for all 4 on their domains.

problems.title: A plane-angle lower bound from projection
problems.question: An equilateral unit triangle projects to A₁B₁C₁ with A₁B₁<√3/2 and A₁C₁<1/2. What necessarily follows about the plane angleθ?
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: Any unit segment in the original plane has projected length at least cosθ. Since A₁C₁<1/2, we have cosθ<1/2.
steps: Thus θ>60°. It also follows that θ>30°, so both listed lower-bound statements are true.
problems.note: The choices “greater than 30°” and “greater than 60°” are both logically necessary; the latter is the more informative answer.

problems.title: Equal projected widths in an isosceles prism
problems.question: A vertical section through M, N on the equal sides of an isosceles triangular prism projects onto the base-side lateral face with are a 12. A second section through midpoint MN parallel to that base side also projects there. Find its projected are a.
problems.idea: Apply trigonometric identities, projection formulas, and a simple spatial model.
formulas: In an isosceles triangle, the horizontal width at a height varies linearly. The horizontal displacement from M on one leg to N on the other equals the full width at their average height.
steps: That average height is the height of midpoint K. Therefore EF equals the horizontal projection length of MN.
Both prism rectangles have the same vertical height, so their projected areas are equal, namely12.
